source.check: returned unopposed: no nomination was received for the division and the retiring member continued (Ballymena Observer, 8 May 1936, p. 10); named as a sitting member of the new council early in the term (Ballymena Observer, 18 September 1936, p. 3: 'O'Donnell' recorded voting in each round of the guardians' vote)

note: Triennial election of Ballymena Rural District Council (and Guardians); nominations received on Wednesday 6 May 1936 by Mr. John Leckey, clerk and returning officer. 'There were only two changes in the personnel of the old Board, viz., in the Kells division, where Joseph Maybin, junr., was nominated in the room of his father, Mr. Joseph Maybin, J.P., and in the Lisnagarron division where Wm. H. Simpson was nominated in the place of his father, Hugh Simpson. Only 18 nominations were received out of the 23 electoral divisions, leaving 5 divisions viz. Tullygarley, Toome, Dunminning, Newtowncrommelin, and Ballyconnelly, as they were, so that the old members for these divisions were declared returned' (Ballymena Observer, 8 May 1936, p. 10, image-read). No poll; the statutory polling day in Co. Antrim was Thursday 4 June 1936. Only the two new members are named in the report, so only Kells and Lisnagarron are recorded (gap-fill 6 Nov 2026). Added from reports of the new council's meetings early in the term, each division inferred from the previous return: Ahoghill, Ballyclug, Ballyconnolly, Broughshane, Clough, Cloughogue, Crumkill, Dunminning, Galgorm, Glenbuck, Glenravel, Glenwherry, Kirkinriola, Longmore, Newtowncrommelin, Portglenone, Slemish, Toome and Tullygarley. Ballyscullion and Drumanaway (round 2, 7 Nov 2026): George Elder and John M'Ateer, members of the old Board after the 1933 members died, sit on the new council from June-July 1936 and are named as the retiring members for those divisions in 1939 (Ballymena Observer, 5 May 1939, p. 10). division inferred from the 1 June 1933 return (Daniel O'Donnell; Ballymena Observer, 5 May 1933, p. 10); the Ballymena Observer, 18 September 1936, p. 3 names the member as sitting for the new council (Ballymena Board of Guardians, September 1936: recorded votes for the appointment of a relieving officer). Also 'Daniel O'Donnell, J.P.' present at the guardians' meeting reported 18 December 1936; he died on 1 July 1939, having 'represented the Toome Division for many years' (Ballymena Observer, 14 July 1939). Deemed re-elected (no nomination).
